newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Regulators silent on SIMEX Taiwan index futures.
newsitem.headline: Regulators silent on SIMEX Taiwan index futures.

text.p: Taiwan's Securities and Exchange Commission declined to comment on Wednesday's surprise announcement by Singapore's SIMEX exchange that it would launch Taiwan stock index futures and options in January.
"We have only just learned about the SIMEX plan," a spokesman for Taiwan's financial watchdog agency said by telephone. "We cannot comment on it until we know more about it."
The SIMEX announced in Singapore on Wednesday that it would launch stock futures and options in January based on the Taiwan stock index compiled by Morgan Stanley Capital International.
The move made SIMEX the second major exchange to unveil plans to tap into Taiwan's liberalising futures market by offering derivatives linked to Taiwan's stock market.

The Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME) won U.S. regulatory approval on December 2 for a similar set of contracts that would be based on the Dow Jones Taiwan Stock Index. Those futures and options will be listed on January 8, the CME has said.

The plans by SIMEX and CME intensify pressure on Taiwan's own planned futures exchange, which is racing to establish itself and list contracts by July 1 but still faces a key obstacle -- lack of a futures exchange law to govern operations.
A draft law has been passed in a Legislative Yuan committee but the full parliament has yet to adopt final legislation with only days left before the year-end recess.
Taiwan's exchange is developing under a cooperation pact with the CME's rival, the Chicago Board of Trade.
The Taiwan Stock Exchange also wants to list index options once it is permitted, but has not settled on trading systems.
"We are studing the software and hardware required to trade the stock index options and we may have it within a few months," an exchange official told Reuters on condition of anonymity.

Such stock exchange options would not require passage of the futures exchange law but would need a reinterpretation of the securities exchange law to include index options under the legal definition of securities, which is not now the case.
Reinterpretation of the securities exchange law is opposed by Taiwan's futures houses, which would prefer to trade in a futures exchange.
Taiwan bans trading in unauthorised financial products but trading in the SIMEX and CME contracts would be hard to block.
Taiwan investors easily could place orders through brokerage houses in Singapore, Hong Kong or other Asian financial centres or even in the United States, local brokers said.
Taiwan futures executives welcomed the SIMEX move and said they hoped Taiwan would accelerate reforms giving them direct legal access to Taiwan index-linked products overseas.

"The government should approve trading of the CME and SIMEX products in Taiwan in order to better monitor the market and protect local investors," Grand Cathay Futures president Steve Wang told Reuters by telephone.

The CME contracts will be listed initially on GLOBEX, its global, round-the-clock electronic trading system. Trading hours will be pegged to those of the Taiwan stock market, including its two-hour Saturday morning session.
Similarly, trading in the SIMEX contracts will commence 15 minutes before Taiwan stock market trading opens and cease 15 minutes after the close.
